source.note: Figures describe the whole linked Matterhorn ski paradise (Zermatt + Breuil-Cervinia + Valtournenche). Lift types per the skiresort.info listing (search summary): 1 cog railway, 2 funiculars, 8 aerial tramways, 11 gondolas, 1 combined gondola/chair installation, 22 chairlifts, 6 T-bars = 51 lifts ('other' = cog railway + 2 funiculars + combined installation; 3 people movers and 7 moving carpets are also listed but not counted in the 51). Uphill capacity 96,074 persons/hour (same listing). Pistes: up to 360 km, of which 74 km blue, 220 km red and 64 km black (search summary); percentages derived from those km (blue = beginner, red = intermediate, black = advanced). Other results: Zermatt alone 52 lifts; Matterhorn ski paradise 54 lifts and 'over 90,000' persons/hour.
Piste reference data — confirm at source. Ski schools and rental shops operate in Zermatt village; other features not on file

character: Car-free village at the foot of the Matterhorn in Valais, with skiing in four sectors (Sunnegga-Rothorn, Gornergrat, Schwarzsee and Matterhorn Glacier Paradise) linked over the Theodul glacier to Breuil-Cervinia and Valtournenche in Italy. The Klein Matterhorn top station (3,883 m) is the highest lift-served point in Europe, and the glacier sector offers summer skiing.
learning: Blue pistes are about a fifth of the linked area's km (74 of about 358 km per the search summary); most terrain is red. Ski schools operate in the village (reference). Confirm beginner zones and lesson products.
